page.title: Partner API
page.introAdmin: Keys for other software to create accounts, sign people in, build and publish apps, and read AI usage, as if those people did it in the studio. A key works either for one reseller's clients or for the platform's own customers, never both, and never for operator or reseller accounts.
page.introReseller: Keys for your own software to create client accounts, sign your clients in, build and publish apps for them, and read their AI usage. A key only ever reaches your own clients, and every build counts against the same allowances as in the studio.

keys.localUrlHelp: Software running on this same server calls this address. Keys set to "This server only" work only here.
keys.publicUrlHelp: Software on other machines calls the public address. Their key must list the machine's IP address.
keys.addBodyAdmin: Choose who the key manages and what it may do. The key is shown once, right after you create it.
keys.addBodyReseller: The key manages your clients only. Choose what it may do. The key is shown once, right after you create it.
keys.name: Name
keys.nameHelp: A name you recognise, such as the software or the team that uses the key.
keys.scopeHelp: A reseller's key reaches only that reseller's clients. A platform key reaches only your own customers who don't belong to a reseller. No key ever reaches operator or reseller accounts.

perm.usersHelp: Create accounts, look them up and list their apps and games.
perm.ssoHelp: Make one-time links that sign a person straight into their workspace.
perm.buildHelp: Plan and build apps and games for a person, using that person's AI allowance, follow their progress, and steer or change a game.
perm.publishHelp: Publish an app's or a game's latest changes to its live address.
perm.usageHelp: Read this month's AI use, per person and in total.

keys.networkLocal: This server only (calls from software on this same machine)
keys.networkLocalHelp: The safest choice. Requests that came in through the internet are refused, even with the right key.
keys.networkList: Only from these IP addresses or ranges
keys.networkListHelp: For software on another machine. List its addresses, such as 203.0.113.10 or 198.51.100.0/24. Add 127.0.0.1 to also allow this server.
keys.createdOnce: Key created. Copy it now: it won't be shown again.
keys.rotatedOnce: New key for {name}. Copy it now: it won't be shown again. The old key has stopped working.
keys.webhookSecretOnce: Saved. Copy the webhook signing secret now: it won't be shown again.
keys.revoked: {name} was revoked. It no longer works.
keys.rotateConfirm: Make a new key for "{name}"? The current key stops working immediately.
keys.revokeConfirm: Revoke "{name}"? Software using it will stop working immediately. This can't be undone.
keys.editHelp: Rename the key or change its permissions, network rule or webhook.
keys.rotateHelp: Replace the key with a new one. The old key stops working at once.
keys.revokeHelp: Turn the key off for good. Software using it stops working at once.
keys.webhookHelp: When a build this key started finishes, a signed message is sent here, so your software doesn't have to keep asking. Must be a public https:// address.
keys.webhookHelpAdmin: When a build this key started finishes, a signed message is sent here, so the software doesn't have to keep asking. https:// addresses, or http:// on a private network.
keys.newWebhookSecretHelp: Replaces the secret the webhook messages are signed with. Update your software with the new one.

manage.forbidden: You don't have access to partner keys.

manage.badIps: These aren't IP addresses or ranges: {list}.
manage.badWebhook: The webhook address must be a public https:// address.
manage.badWebhookAdmin: The webhook address must start with https:// or http://.
